title: Tokenized deposits — interactive explainer
learning_objective: Show how the token's legal meaning, authoritative ledger, accounting state and settlement design change who owes the money and when a transfer can be treated as complete.
audience: Mixed executive, banking, legal and technical audience

data.source: Project research notes and linked primary sources; no live data

assumptions: CHF amounts are illustrative and not market data.
Cross-border examples use a fixed illustrative 1 CHF = 1 EUR rate.
Legal, accounting and finality outcomes are model-dependent and require product-specific review.
A successful DLT event is not presented as interbank settlement finality, a transfer of the debtor, or a final customer credit unless the relevant workflow status confirms it.
Stablecoin backing is illustrative evidence only; it is not a statement of reserve composition, guarantee terms, audit status or deposit protection.
The conditional-payment milestone and verifier are illustrative; production terms must define the evidence, authority, expiry and dispute process.
The Agorá five-stage scenario adapts the report-era workflow pattern to this explainer; it does not reproduce Agorá’s platform-authoritative architecture.

validation.scope: Deterministic state checks for the high-priority settlement, failure and representation boundaries, the conditional-payment lifecycle and the Agorá five-stage workflow.
